Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 50-year-old man with 4–5 days of cough (mainly dry, occasional “mucky” phlegm), rhinorrhoea, sore throat, subjective fevers/rigors, myalgias, transient diarrhoea, and increasing shortness of breath.  
• Past history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension; overweight; occasional smoker and moderate alcohol intake.  
• Most consistent with an acute viral upper respiratory infection/influenza-like illness (including possible COVID-19).  
• Bacterial lower respiratory tract infection (community-acquired pneumonia or acute bronchitis) considered due to sputum production and dyspnoea; clinician provided delayed antibiotic prescription.  
• No red-flag features for pulmonary embolism, heart failure exacerbation, or ACE-inhibitor cough at present.  

Management Plan
- Symptomatic care: rest, maintain hydration, regular Paracetamol for fever and myalgias  
- Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily to start if no improvement or worsening in 24–48 h (dose/strength not documented)  
- Safety-net advice: return for review if symptoms worsen, persistent dyspnoea, new chest pain, or no improvement after one week  
- Lifestyle advice: continue efforts to quit smoking/vaping transition; limit alcohol intake  
- Discussed monitoring of diabetes control during illness; no changes to current Metformin and Lisinopril therapy  
- Follow-up: routine GP review if antibiotic course started or if symptoms persist

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection / Influenza-like illness (incl. COVID-19) – High likelihood: abrupt onset, constellation of upper-airway symptoms, myalgias, feverishness.  
2. Community-acquired pneumonia – Moderate likelihood: productive sputum, subjective fever, dyspnoea, comorbid diabetes; no exam/vitals to confirm.  
3. Acute bronchitis – Moderate likelihood: sub-acute cough following URI; overlaps with above.
